title: What the State housing department wrote to San Francisco, 2021-2026
question: Did the State find that San Francisco broke housing law, and was it put right?
finding: 15 letters on file. 4 record an adverse finding: 2021-11-22 San Francisco – Letter of Inquiry and Technical Support (violation found); 2022-12-29 3832 18th Street Project – Notice of Violation (violation found); 2023-10-26 Review of San Francisco’s Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) Ordinance unde (does not comply); 2023-11-28 City and County of San Francisco – Corrective Action Letter (overdue actions found; corrective action required). The 28 November 2023 findings were closed on 16 January 2024, when the State found the overdue actions done.
how: Each PDF linked from the State's enforcement-letters dashboard filtered to San Francisco was read; the verdict is taken from the letter's own words (violated, does not comply, failed to timely implement, successful completion).
limits: These are planning-law letters, about how the City approves housing, not about how it spends money. A letter of inquiry or technical assistance is not a finding. The dashboard lists 17 entries, two pairs sharing one PDF.
